{
  "proposals": [
    {
      "title": "Batched time-step rainfall-runoff simulation on GPUs for ensemble likelihood evaluation",
      "field": "Computational hydrology and rainfall-runoff model calibration",
      "sequential_part": "Within one parameter proposal, the watershed state must be updated recursively through daily time steps; each state depends on the previous day.",
      "restructure": "Keep the daily recurrence exactly but vectorize the state update over thousands of parameter sets or catchments on a GPU, so the sequential time loop becomes a short sequence of wide parallel kernels.",
      "condition": "Concurrent parameter sets number in the hundreds to thousands so the per-step update saturates GPU throughput, and CPU-GPU transfer cost is amortized across many likelihood evaluations.",
      "baselines": "Single-thread CPU and OpenMP multi-core runs of the same solver; compare wall-clock time and numerical agreement of streamflow and objective values within a set tolerance.",
      "first_test": "Benchmark one model with 1024 parameter sets over 30 years of daily forcing data on CPU vs GPU; roughly 30-60 minutes of GPU time."
    },
    {
      "title": "Many short independent MCMC chains with rank-normalized early stopping",
      "field": "Bayesian inference for hydrological model calibration",
      "sequential_part": "A single MCMC chain is inherently sequential; every sample waits on the previous accepted sample, so long chains cannot be shortened naively.",
      "restructure": "Replace one long chain with hundreds of independent chains launched together on a GPU, using vectorized log-likelihood calls, then pool draws after burn-in and monitor rank-normalized R-hat and effective sample size.",
      "condition": "The posterior basin supports mixing across seeds, proposal scales can be tuned or adapted, and GPU memory is sufficient for many chains; isolated modes are handled with multiple seeds or tempering if present.",
      "baselines": "A single long CPU chain with equal total iterations; compare R-hat, ESS per GPU-second, posterior parameter summaries, and predictive streamflow uncertainty intervals.",
      "first_test": "Run 200 chains for 5000 iterations on a small existing rainfall-runoff posterior; roughly 1-2 GPU-hours."
    },
    {
      "title": "Speculative multi-branch proposal evaluation for sequential-hazard MCMC",
      "field": "Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms applied to Bayesian calibration",
      "sequential_part": "The accept/reject decision at step t determines the starting point for step t+1, so the chain cannot evaluate the next proposal until the current decision is made.",
      "restructure": "At each step evaluate k candidate proposals from the current state in parallel on the GPU, then combine them via a statistically valid multi-proposal Metropolis-Hastings update, or use branch-and-rollback prefetching to reuse speculative evaluations.",
      "condition": "Log-likelihood evaluation dominates the runtime, and the acceptance rate and proposal diversity are high enough that parallel branches are useful for the chosen kernel.",
      "baselines": "Single-proposal Metropolis-Hastings with the same rainfall-runoff likelihood; compare effective sample size per GPU-second and posterior summary accuracy, and report wasted speculative evaluations.",
      "first_test": "Test the multi-proposal kernel on a cheap analytic proxy for the hydrologic posterior plus one batched likelihood run; measure candidates per accepted draw; roughly 1 GPU-hour."
    },
    {
      "title": "Neural likelihood emulator for accelerating rainfall-runoff calibration",
      "field": "Scientific machine learning for hydrological model calibration",
      "sequential_part": "Every MCMC likelihood call requires a multi-year rainfall-runoff simulation with sequential daily recurrence, and a long chain needs millions of such calls.",
      "restructure": "Build a GPU neural surrogate mapping parameters to likelihood values or summary signatures from offline simulator runs; evaluate the surrogate in large batches during MCMC, with periodic exact simulator re-evaluation to correct or diagnose drift.",
      "condition": "The surrogate is accurate inside the high-posterior region, its error is small relative to posterior width, and offline training runs cover the relevant prior or exploratory posterior region.",
      "baselines": "Exact simulator MCMC runs; compare posterior means, covariances, predictive intervals, and wall-clock time, and explicitly measure emulator-induced posterior shift.",
      "first_test": "Generate 10,000 offline simulator runs for one catchment, train a small MLP or Gaussian process, and measure validation error and prediction speedup; roughly 2-4 GPU-hours including data generation."
    },
    {
      "title": "Differentiable gradient-based HMC on GPUs to shorten sequential chains",
      "field": "Differentiable Bayesian inference for rainfall-runoff models",
      "sequential_part": "Random-walk Metropolis chains need very long sequential mixing because proposal directions are inefficient in high-dimensional parameter space.",
      "restructure": "Rewrite the rainfall-runoff recurrence in a differentiable framework and reverse-mode autodifferentiate the log-likelihood; run HMC or NUTS on GPU with multiple leapfrog trajectories in parallel, taking fewer sequential steps to reach the same effective sample size.",
      "condition": "The model and log-likelihood are differentiable with stable gradients, threshold or staircase terms can be smoothed, and GPU memory holds several leapfrog trajectories at once.",
      "baselines": "Existing random-walk Metropolis or DE-MC chains on CPU; compare effective sample size per second, posterior summary accuracy, and leapfrog energy diagnostics.",
      "first_test": "Implement a differentiable single-catchment model, check gradients with finite differences, and benchmark 100 warm-up HMC trajectories; roughly 1 GPU-hour."
    }
  ]
}
